event.title: Missouri May Revert to Previous Congressional Districts After Court Ruling
event.canonical_title: Missouri May Revert to Previous Congressional Districts After Court Ruling
event.summary: Missouri is set to revert to its former congressional districts following a court decision that rejected a map backed by Trump. This ruling could lead to a unique situation where the state runs the November general election with different US House districts than those used in the August primary, potentially affecting over a million voters.

timeline.summary: The US Supreme Court is set to hear a case regarding Missouri's congressional map for the third time. A federal appeals court previously sided with Republicans who aim to utilize district boundaries redrawn last year, which are believed to provide an advantage to the GOP in the upcoming midterm elections.

event_overview.title: About Congressional Redistricting
event_overview.subject: Congressional Redistricting
event_overview.summary: Congressional redistricting is the process of setting the boundaries for Missouri’s eight U.S. House districts. This dispute concerns a mid-decade map enacted as House Bill 1 in 2025, a voter referendum challenging that law, and overlapping state and federal court proceedings over which map may govern the 2026 general election.

facts.label: Representation
facts.value: Missouri is divided into eight congressional districts for elections to the U.S. House of Representatives.

facts.label: Competing maps
facts.value: The earlier congressional plan was enacted in 2022; House Bill 1, enacted during the Missouri General Assembly’s 2025 Second Extraordinary Session, established a replacement set of congressional-district boundaries.

facts.label: Referendum process
facts.value: Missouri’s constitution permits a referendum on most laws through petitions signed by 5% of legal voters in each of two-thirds of the state’s congressional districts, with petitions due within 90 days after final adjournment of the session that passed the bill.

facts.label: State-court ruling
facts.value: On September 3, 2026, the Supreme Court of Missouri held that the referendum petition against HB 1 was legal, sufficient, and timely; it ruled that HB 1 would not take effect unless approved by voters and that the 2022 districts remained in force for the November 2026 general election.

facts.label: Federal litigation
facts.value: The related federal case concerns whether federal constitutional provisions require use of the 2025 map despite the state referendum ruling. On September 10, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court stayed a September 8 federal district-court order while appellate proceedings continued.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the September 2026 court actions affecting which congressional map could be used for the general election, not Missouri’s full redistricting history or every related lawsuit and election-administration step.
